youtube.title: What If You Healed Like a GTA 6 Character? #Shorts
youtube.description:
What if you healed like a GTA 6 character? Eat a snack, and your health bar is full again. Remy runs three tests on how a real body does it.

Test 1, a small cut: it usually closes in about a week, but underneath your body keeps rebuilding for months. Healed scar tissue is only about 80% as strong as the skin was before.
Test 2, giving blood: your body replaces the liquid part of your blood (plasma) in about a day, but the red blood cells take about 4 to 6 weeks. That's why blood banks make whole-blood donors wait at least 8 weeks between donations.
Test 3, a broken arm: a simple broken bone usually needs about 6 to 8 weeks to heal; a bad break can take months.

No snack fixes that in seconds. Rest, good food and sleep help your body do the work. In the game, you heal in seconds. In real life, your body is quietly fixing you every single day. What's the slowest thing you ever had to heal from?

Sources:
- Wound healing stages (minor cuts close in about 7-10 days; remodelling goes on for months): HealthPartners: https://www.healthpartners.com/blog/wound-healing-stages-how-to-tell-if-a-wound-is-healing-infected-or-chronic/ , Cedars-Sinai: https://www.cedars-sinai.org/health-topics/how-wounds-heal , MedlinePlus: https://medlineplus.gov/ency/patientinstructions/000741.htm
- Scar tissue about 80% as strong as the original skin: Marshfield Clinic: https://shine365.marshfieldclinic.org/wellness/scars , KidsHealth: https://kidshealth.org/en/kids/scars.html
- Plasma replaced in about 24 hours, red cells in about 4-6 weeks, at least 8 weeks (56 days) between whole-blood donations: American Red Cross: https://redcrossblood.org/faq.html , NHS Blood and Transplant: https://www.blood.co.uk/the-donation-process/after-your-donation/how-your-body-replaces-blood/ , Stanford Blood Center: https://stanfordbloodcenter.org/pulse-spring23-what-really-happens-to-your-body-after-you-donate-blood-effects-risks-and-recovery/
- Minor fractures heal in about 6-8 weeks, severe fractures 3-6 months: NHS Sherwood Forest Hospitals: https://www.sfh-tr.nhs.uk/media/16693/pil202308-01-fra-fractures.pdf , Royal Osteoporosis Society: https://theros.org.uk/information-and-support/osteoporosis/living-with-osteoporosis/recovering-from-a-broken-bone/

Not medical advice. For an injury, ask a doctor or nurse.
